The finite coincidence identity follows from exchangeable extreme labels. Splitting \(A_p=p/S_1+B_p\) with \(\mathbb E B_p=-p\log p\) yields the \(p t e^{-t}\) tail. value.rationale: The leading spherical width of \(P_{G(n,p)}\) agrees with K_n, while its second-order law nontrivially retains \(p\) via a reciprocal-arrival-time Gumbel mixture and sharp upper-tail constant. The theorem strengthens annealed convergence to almost-sure graph-quenched self-averaging, a meaningful geometric distinction for a natural family of random lattice polytopes. Its exact finite width-coincidence identity directly connects random linear optimization to edge density, without arbitrarily chosen finite parameters.
